newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas edges higher on colder weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas edges higher on colder weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices climbed another five cents Wednesday, as buyers re-emerged in anticipation of colder weather in the U.S. this weekend and into next week, market sources said.
Swing prices on the Gulf Coast pipes rose by more than five cents to the low-to-mid $2.60s, with Henry Hub, La., quoted mostly in the mid-$2.60s.

Prices were equally higher in south Texas, where traders reported closing deals mostly in the mid-$2.40s. Temperatures in Texas are expected to dip to slightly below-normal levels Thursday and Friday but then return to normal by Sunday.

Also tightening supply in Texas is the scheduled outage at Houston Light and Power's South Texas 2 nuclear power plant. The 1,250 megawatt unit is expected to go off line this Friday for about 35 days of maintenance and refueling.
Further East, where cooler temperatures are forecast to arrive this weekend, New York city-gate prices climbed into the $3.00-3.15 range.
Similarly on the Appalachian pipes, prices for Thursday delivery firmed by more than five cents to the mid-to-high $2.80s.
The stronger Gulf values filtered into the Midcontinent market, where most deals were confirmed done at about a five-cent premium to Tuesday's values around $2.50.
Chicago city-gate values were also talked marginally higher in the $2.75-2.85 range.

Temperatures in the Midcontinent are expected to remain near- to above-normal through early next week despite a brief cold spell early this weekend. Below-normal temperatures are forecast to return later next week, Weather Services Corp reported.
In west Texas, Permian prices gained another five cents to about $2.40, while Waha deals were reported done mostly in the mid-$2.40s.

Swing prices at the southern California border were about 10 cents higher in the high-$2.40s to low-$2.50s. Late deals were reported done in the mid-$2.50s as Canadian supplies became tighter, traders said.

Withdrawal estimates for this afternoon's American Gas Association weekly storage report are in the 155-180 bcf range, as compared with a 213 bcf drawdown a year ago. ((--H McCulloch, New York Power Desk +212-859-1628))
